The child struggled with tool selection and sequence, incorrectly assuming the hammer was needed to open the sealed box and assemble parts, while the instructions required using the screwdriver for assembly. The caregiver clarified that the hammer was not needed for assembly—only the screwdriver—and demonstrated proper use of the screwdriver to attach the shelves; however, the child failed to correct their approach, resulting in incomplete assembly.
  2. The task was to sweep the living room floor, a level 1 cleaning task, using a broom and dustpan. The child initially hesitated on tool coordination but, unlike in past experiences with tool misuse, correctly used the broom to gather debris and the dustpan to collect it after the caregiver modeled proper technique. The task was completed successfully.
